title: Sixteen Vocalion sides with Austin and his cornet records
summary: He recalls the Vocalion sides, his cornet playing, and the theme tune from WSMB.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Did you ever play play play night on any records?
Yeah, with Austin. But I never... I asked Bill about that. You remember I asked you about that a long time ago?

The day that I left Austin, see we were supposed to go to Europe. And I wanted to come home before I went to Europe and they were gonna go up and down the west coast playing vaudeville, you see. And I didn't want to do that so I told him I said well I'll go home and I'll meet you in New York. We were supposed to go to England because he had been a big hit over there at one time. And so the day that I left, the day before I left rather, we made 16 sides for Vocalion. Now the only one I ever heard, and I made 8 of those I made on cornet. And the only one that I ever heard was Chinatown. The tune. China. That's the only one I ever heard. Now I asked you, I asked a hundred people, you know, try to find them for me. Cause it's the only things I ever made on cornet. I mean on a professional label on the witch corn. Now I gotta, I gotta think back there that I played the blues with Martha Boswell playing the organ. You know these little church organs, like little home organs like that. We played the blues. She playing the organ and me playing the cornet. Then I got that thing that I, I don't know whether you gonna like this or not Richard. I don't like to say these things but they're true. That thing that you, that the original, your theme song. Oh yeah. Yeah, your, your, your, I made the original on that. Oh but, Joe Mareza's got it, it was made up at WSMB. With Johnny? Yeah. That's my tune.
Oh. Well, what about Perini? You recorded it too.
Yeah, but mellophone. I didn't make any, any cornet.
